title: Emergence Quantum and AirTrunk Partner to Develop Hyperscale Cryogenic Data Center Infrastructure - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Emergence Quantum, a 2025 University of Sydney spin-out building cryogenic control electronics, signed an MOU with Asia-Pacific hyperscaler AirTrunk to engineer campus-scale cryogenic cooling for sub-100 K CMOS logic, superconducting interconnects and fault-tolerant QPUs inside commercial data halls. The framing is notable: the near-term payoff is pitched at AI/HPC thermal and power bottlenecks (tokens/watt, leakage current), with quantum-readiness as the long-tail option, and it extends to liquid air energy storage and the elimination of evaporative water cooling towers.

themes.theme: Cryo-classical as the near-term AI play

insights.claim: Emergence Quantum and AirTrunk are justifying cryogenic data center R&D primarily on classical AI/HPC economics — operating silicon logic below 100 Kelvin to improve electron mobility and clock speeds while suppressing leakage power and thermal noise — rather than on quantum computing demand alone.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryogenic cooling vendors may find their first real revenue in AI data centers, not quantum — watch for cryo-CMOS line items appearing in hyperscaler capex before any quantum deployment does.
insights.quote: Operating silicon logic at cryogenic temperatures improves electron mobility and clock speeds while suppressing leakage power and thermal noise.
insights.locator: The joint R&D initiative addresses physical scaling

insights.claim: The stated performance metric for cryogenic classical compute is the tokens-per-watt ratio, explicitly tying sub-100 K transistor operation to large-language-model inference economics rather than to scientific computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If tokens/watt is the sales pitch, cryogenic infrastructure competes directly with liquid-cooling and custom-silicon vendors for the same AI efficiency budget.

insights.claim: Superconducting interconnects are claimed to show 10,000x lower electrical resistance than copper wiring at 10 GHz, positioned as a fix for data transfer bottlenecks between QPU, GPU and memory clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A credible 10,000x interconnect resistance advantage would attack the memory-bandwidth wall that currently caps GPU cluster scaling — a direct threat vector to copper-based interconnect and optical-interconnect suppliers.
insights.quote: at 10 GHz frequencies, superconducting interconnects exhibit 10,000× lower electrical resistance compared to traditional copper wiring

insights.claim: The Emergence Quantum-AirTrunk framework evaluates closed-loop liquid air cooling as a replacement for evaporative water cooling towers, targeting the water-consumption constraint that increasingly blocks data center permitting.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Water-free cooling is becoming a siting prerequisite in drought-exposed regions; approaches that eliminate evaporative towers raise the option value of otherwise unbuildable campuses.
insights.quote: closed-loop liquid air cooling to replace evaporative water cooling towers

insights.claim: Liquid air energy storage (LAES) is being scoped inside the same data center design for gigawatt-scale grid balancing, meaning the cryogenic plant doubles as an energy-storage asset rather than being pure cooling overhead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Bundling storage revenue with cooling capex changes the ROI math for cryogenic facilities and puts LAES players in the data center supply chain alongside battery vendors.
insights.quote: liquid air energy storage (LAES) for gigawatt-scale grid balancing

insights.claim: The partnership's scope extends to direct cryogenic carbon capture, folding an emissions-abatement mechanism into the cooling infrastructure itself.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An ESG-adjacent secondary use case that could unlock subsidy or offset financing, but it is listed as an evaluation item rather than a committed deliverable.

insights.claim: Emergence Quantum's cryo-control and readout wiring is deliberately qubit-agnostic, designed to host spin, superconducting, trapped-ion and photonic QPUs in the same data hall rather than betting on one modality winning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modality-neutral picks-and-shovels suppliers capture value regardless of which qubit technology wins — a lower-variance exposure than backing a single hardware architecture.

insights.claim: The agreement is a Memorandum of Understanding rather than a binding supply or construction contract, so no capacity, capex or timeline commitments are disclosed.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Treat this as optionality signaling, not booked revenue; the conversion of the MOU into a funded pilot campus is the milestone worth waiting for.
insights.quote: has executed a strategic partnership Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
insights.locator: Quantum control hardware startup Emergence Quantum

insights.claim: Emergence Quantum is a 2025 University of Sydney spin-out led by co-founders Professor David Reilly and Professor Thomas Ohki, specializing in cryogenic control electronics and qubit-agnostic wiring interfaces.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An extremely young private company is being handed a design role with a major hyperscaler — a credibility marker for academic cryo-electronics spin-outs as acquisition or partnership targets.
insights.locator: Led by co-founders Professor David Reilly

insights.claim: The explicit commercial goal is a repeatable blueprint for 'quantum-ready' hyperscale facilities that monetizes cryo-classical HPC acceleration in the interim while preserving an upgrade path to fault-tolerant quantum deployments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A bridge-revenue strategy is how quantum infrastructure survives a long commercialization timeline; look for competing hyperscalers to announce similar quantum-ready campus standards.
insights.quote: establish a commercial blueprint for “quantum-ready” hyperscale facilities
